curation_note: Every numeric parameter below carries an `origin` tag. `fitted` means SYNTHBODY estimated it itself from the named observed dataset using the estimator in synthbody.engine.analysis.estimation, and the value is reproducible by running scripts/run_validation.py. `illustrative` means the number was chosen to make the software demonstrable and is NOT evidence. Nothing here is a dosing recommendation.

parameter_origin_legend.measured: Directly measured or reported population value from a cited primary source.
parameter_origin_legend.fitted: Estimated by SYNTHBODY regression against a named observed dataset shipped with the platform.
parameter_origin_legend.literature_fitted: A fitted estimate reported by a cited publication, not re-estimated here.
parameter_origin_legend.derived: Computed from other parameters by an explicit documented equation.
parameter_origin_legend.inferred: Reasoned from related data or widely quoted values whose primary source SYNTHBODY did not retrieve.
parameter_origin_legend.illustrative: A plausible default chosen for demonstrability. Not evidence.
parameter_origin_legend.user: Supplied by the operator at run time.

drugs.name: Theophylline
drugs.mechanism_summary: Non-selective phosphodiesterase inhibitor and adenosine receptor antagonist producing bronchodilation.
drugs.primary_elimination: Hepatic metabolism, predominantly CYP1A2 (approximately 90%), with a small renal contribution.
drugs.why_this_drug: Chosen as SYNTHBODY's reference compound because it has a well-characterised one-compartment first-order-absorption structure AND a publicly redistributable observed concentration-time dataset, which together make genuine held-out validation possible. Its narrow therapeutic index also makes dose comparison a meaningful exercise.
drugs.validation_note: The one-compartment model parameters below were estimated from Theoph subjects 1,3,5,7,9,11 and evaluated on held-out subjects 2,4,6,8,10,12. See the Validation workspace for the achieved statistics.

pk_1cmt_foa.note: Multiply CL_per_kg and V_per_kg by body weight to obtain the model's CL (L/h) and V (L). Because the source data are oral-only, bioavailability is not identifiable and was fixed at 1; CL and V are therefore apparent values (CL/F, V/F).

CL_per_kg.description: Apparent oral clearance per kilogram body weight.
CL_per_kg.corroboration: Independently consistent with the widely reported adult theophylline clearance of approximately 0.04 L/h/kg. This agreement was not used in the estimation.

V_per_kg.description: Apparent volume of distribution per kilogram body weight.
V_per_kg.corroboration: Independently consistent with the widely reported adult theophylline volume of distribution of approximately 0.5 L/kg. This agreement was not used in the estimation.

ka.caveat: The between-subject CV of 121% is very large and two calibration subjects returned relative standard errors above 300% for this parameter. ka is poorly determined by this sampling schedule. Treat absorption-phase predictions with corresponding scepticism.

F.description: Bioavailability fixed at 1 because it is not identifiable from oral-only data. This is a structural choice, not a measurement; it is why CL and V above are apparent values.

pbpk_perfusion_limited.note: Inputs to the perfusion-limited PBPK model. The PBPK model is RESEARCH ONLY and has not been validated against observed concentration-time data.

logP.description: Octanol:water partition coefficient used for tissue-composition partitioning.
logP.caveat: This is PubChem's XLogP3 value, which is a COMPUTED descriptor, not an experimentally measured log P. It is used here as the best openly available estimate and labelled accordingly.

fu_p.caveat: Theophylline is commonly described as approximately 40% plasma-protein bound, implying fu of about 0.6. SYNTHBODY did not retrieve a primary measurement of this value, so it is labelled inferred rather than measured.

BP.caveat: No primary source for this value was retrieved. It is a plausible default for a small neutral molecule with limited erythrocyte partitioning and must not be treated as a measurement.

CLint_H.description: Hepatic intrinsic clearance on unbound drug.
CLint_H.caveat: Chosen so the resulting well-stirred hepatic clearance is of a plausible order for theophylline. It was NOT back-calculated from the validated compartmental clearance and is not a measurement.

CL_R.caveat: Reflects only the qualitative fact that theophylline has a minor renal elimination route. Not a measured value.

pd_model.response_variable: Bronchodilation, expressed as percent improvement in FEV1 from baseline
pd_model.caveat: EVERY parameter in this pharmacodynamic model is illustrative. SYNTHBODY ships no pharmacodynamic dataset for theophylline and did not extract concentration-effect values from any publication. The curve demonstrates that the PK/PD machinery works; it is not a prediction of bronchodilator response. The cited study established that theophylline bronchodilation increases with concentration across roughly the 5-20 mg/L range, which is the only claim being relied on.

reference_concentration_band.label: Historical therapeutic range
reference_concentration_band.caveat: The 10-20 mg/L range is the historical target. It is actively contested: later clinical opinion favours lower targets (roughly 5-15 mg/L) because toxicity rises steeply above 20 mg/L. SYNTHBODY presents this as an adjustable reference band, not a clinical target, and does not recommend any concentration.

body_weight.method: Parameters are per-kilogram, so body weight scales them linearly. An allometric option (CL to the 0.75 power) is available in the Patient Builder.

smoking_status.caveat: Direction is well established (CYP1A2 induction raises theophylline clearance). The 1.6x magnitude is a commonly quoted order of magnitude that SYNTHBODY did not extract from a primary source.

hepatic_function.caveat: Direction is supported by the cited studies; these specific multipliers are SYNTHBODY defaults and are not measurements.

default_regimen.note: Matches the single 300 mg oral dose design of the Theoph study, which is the only design for which this model has been validated.

random_effects.note: From the two-stage fit; an upper bound on true between-subject variability.
Very poorly determined; see the ka caveat.

residual_error.caveat: A plausible assay error model, not estimated from the data. Used only when residual error is explicitly requested.

limitations: Validated only for a single oral dose in healthy adults over about 25 hours.
No validation for intravenous administration, multiple dosing, children, the elderly, hepatic impairment or drug interactions, despite the software permitting all of those simulations.
Bioavailability is fixed, so clearance and volume are apparent values.
The absorption rate constant is poorly determined by the source sampling schedule.

drugs.name: Indomethacin
drugs.primary_elimination: Hepatic metabolism and glucuronidation with enterohepatic recirculation.
drugs.why_this_drug: Chosen as SYNTHBODY's second validation compound because its publicly redistributable intravenous dataset shows a clear biexponential decline, which exercises the two-compartment model structure that theophylline's oral data cannot.
drugs.validation_note: Parameters estimated from Indometh subjects 1,3,5 and evaluated on held-out subjects 2,4,6.

pk_2cmt.note: CRITICAL: the administered dose is absent from the distributed Indometh dataset. SYNTHBODY used a nominal dose of 1 unit, so the volumes and clearances below are APPARENT VALUES PER UNIT DOSE, not absolute L or L/h. Rate constants and the distribution/elimination ratios derived from them remain valid; absolute volumes do not.

CL.description: Apparent total clearance per unit dose.

V1.description: Apparent central volume per unit dose.

Q.description: Apparent intercompartmental clearance per unit dose.

V2.description: Apparent peripheral volume per unit dose.
V2.caveat: The reported between-subject CV of 3.55% is implausibly small for a peripheral volume and reflects only three calibration subjects, one of which had a relative standard error of 81% on this parameter. Do not read it as evidence that V2 is tightly conserved.

ka.description: Zero: the model is used intravenously only for this drug.

default_regimen.note: A nominal 1-unit dose, matching the unknown-dose parameterisation. Changing the dose scales concentrations linearly and does not make the absolute values meaningful.

random_effects.note: From three calibration subjects; very imprecise.
From three calibration subjects; very imprecise.

limitations: ABSOLUTE VOLUMES AND CLEARANCES ARE NOT RECOVERABLE because the dataset omits the dose.
The source study reports enterohepatic recirculation, which the two-compartment structure cannot represent; this contributes irreducible fit error.
Only three calibration subjects, so the typical values and especially the variability estimates are very imprecise.
Eight hours of sampling under-determines the terminal phase.

drugs.name: Capacity-limited demonstration compound
drugs.why_this_drug: A deliberately synthetic compound used to exercise the Michaelis-Menten model and to demonstrate why saturable elimination makes dose increments dangerous. Labelled as synthetic everywhere it appears.
drugs.validation_note: THIS IS NOT A REAL DRUG. All parameters are invented to produce visibly non-linear behaviour. Nothing about this entry corresponds to any compound, and no output from it means anything clinically. It exists to demonstrate the non-linear solver path and the saturation diagnostics.

default_regimen.note: Multiple dosing is used here on purpose: it is where capacity-limited elimination produces disproportionate accumulation. Try raising the dose by 50% and watch exposure more than double.

limitations: NOT A REAL DRUG. Every number is invented.
No observed data exists for this compound because it does not exist.
Use it to test the engine, never to reason about pharmacology.
